respawn problem
Imagine a game mechanic operating in everyday life.

ok so you respawn but your stuff doesnt. first death you lose a phone. annoying but fine. second you lose your house keys. now you cant get in to get the spare phone. third you deliberately die outside your own front door so someone will find you and call an ambulance and open the door but you forgot you respawn at the bus station. why the bus station. thats where you last sat down long enough to save. except you didnt know sitting was saving so you've been standing for two days because you dont want to overwrite it with somewhere worse like the toilets at work. i think the intresting bit is you could use this to go places free, just get there die respawn but no thats the oppsite direction. wait. you need to save at the destination first. which means you have already got there. this is a terrible superpower. also theres now three of your bodies about and the police have a lot of questions and your mum keeps getting calls. you cant phone her because of the first phone. really should have started by putting the phone down
waiting room
Time stops, but only for part of a room.
time stopped at my waist so my legs are in yesterday. i can lean really far forward but not stand up. dont know if im hungry now or yesterday hungry. nurse says please stay seated. way ahead of you
allotment seven
A gardener finds something unexpected in the soil.

Dug up a spoon, two batteries and then a jaw. Bottom bit with teeth. I fetched Mr Bell. He said fox. I said it's got fillings. He took his glasses out. After a bit he brought a bucket. I didn't think we should move it. He said we couldn't leave it for the children. No children there but I understood. Rang the allotment number. A woman asked whether I'd paid my fees. I said yes and tried again about the teeth.
tomatoes attempt
Describe a task you have put off.

Need to tie the tomatoes up. They are lying all over each other. I had a story about someone hiding in the greenhouse but now all I can think is I should actually go and tie them up before it rains. Got string somewhere. Blue string.
stop watering it
Give practical advice you wish someone would follow.

Please stop watering it every time you visit. Three of us keep watering the same plant and its basically living in a puddle. I put a note on it and Dad watered the note. Not on purpose. He thought the soil looked dry at the top. It IS dry at the top because there's an inch of decorative stones on top. Under that its soup. I've taken it out of the pot now and put newspaper round the roots. The kitchen looks like a very small crime scene but I think it might live.
Room 206
A hotel guest hears someone enter the wrong room.

The key turned at 2:11. I was awake because of the pipe over the bed. A man came in carrying his shoes. He saw me, stopped, looked at the door number from the inside as though it might be written there. I said wrong room. He said no. We waited. He put his shoes down very carefully and went into the bathroom. I could hear him opening the cupboard. My phone was on the desk beyond him. I got out on the other side of the bed, kept the mattress between us. When he came out he was holding a woman's bracelet. He said where is she. I said I checked in at nine. He looked at the empty half of the bed and sat on the floor.
Fire route
A person escapes a building by an unfamiliar exit.

Smoke in the corridor. Not thick, just enough to hide the far door. Kit crawled with one hand against the skirting board. Room numbers were useless down there. She counted doorways instead. Four, five, the stair should be next. Her hand found a gap and she pushed through onto cold concrete. No smoke here. She stood and started down. At the first landing the door was locked. At the second, chained. She kept going. The alarm sounded distant now, above her, and the steps were wet. There was a light under the next door. She hammered with both hands. Someone on the other side said we're closed. She screamed fire and the voice said we know.
Two minutes
Write a suspense scene using only physical actions.

He tried the handle. She put her foot against the door. He pushed harder. The chair slid backwards across the carpet. She reached behind her for the phone and knocked it off the table. It rang once on the floor. He stopped pushing.
checkout at eleven
A night worker finishes a difficult shift.

He had vomited in the plant pot and offered me twenty pounds to say it was there already. I told him keep the twenty, get a taxi. His friend was asleep against the luggage rack. We got the friend up between us and out through the revolving door, which took longer than it should have. At the kerb the sick one started crying. He said it had been a terrible wedding. I said most of them were by this time. That wasn't a professional thing to say but he laughed. I got their bags in the boot and went back for a bucket. At six the day porter asked if it had been quiet. I said more or less.
lifting the sofa
Help someone move something they should have measured.

Got the sofa stuck on the stairs. It went up so must come down, she said, but her husband had taken the bannister off and neither of us had tools. The new sofa was on the pavement. Started raining. A boy waiting for his bus helped push the old one back upstairs. Missed his bus. I drove him to school. He asked if I was family. Said no, next door. He said I should have pretended I was out. He was late for maths and I think quite pleased.
at the clinic
Someone tries to help but misunderstands the situation.

I thought she couldn't read the form. She kept turning it over, looking at the back, so I offered. She said she could read perfectly well. I felt awful. Then she asked me what counts as next of kin if you don't speak to any of them. I didn't know. My form was already filled in with my sister's name and I covered that bit with my hand which made no sense. I said maybe put a friend. She said the friend is why I'm here. We sat there. I wish I'd said something better. The nurse called a name that might have been hers and she got up without her bag and I had to run after her with it.
the sandwich question
Write a complaint that turns into an unrelated confession.

Why does every sandwich have to be wet now. You ask for cheese and they give you cheese plus a substance. Mayo or chutney or something green that has a special name. I just want bread and cheese and maybe I'm the boring one but I am the one paying six pounds. Anyway this is not actually about sandwiches I'm annoyed because I ate lunch in the car again and said I was busy so nobody would ask why. I'm not busy I just can't keep up with the conversation in there. Everyone knows a programme I haven't watched. I could watch it. There are nine seasons. I don't want to give nine seasons of my life to having something to say while I eat wet bread.
smoke alarm
A person cooks something far beyond their abilities.

The recipie says sear, I have seared. The entire flat is seared. I've got both windows open and a towel under the alarm and my brother is telling me you don't put a towel under an alarm, I'm not putting it under it I'm WAVING it. The steak is black outside and cold in the middle. I know because I cut it, which apparantly you shouldn't do either. Everyone is an expert after you've done something. He suggests the oven. Fine. Where's the tray. We use a cake tin. There is birthday glitter in it. He says it won't matter. I turn the oven on and realise the potatoes were supposed to be in there forty minutes ago. We are going to eat at ten. At the earliest.
still cold
Write a tiny attempt about an uninteresting moment.

tea went cold. made another one. also cold. I keep trying to think of an interesting reason but there isnt one I was watching videos of a man pressure washing a driveway and lost half an hour. could have been worse driveways I suppose
not our house
Remember entering a place that looked familiar.

We went into the wrong house. Same estate, same brown doors. Dad walked in so I went straight upstairs. Sat on what I thought was my bed. There were different posters. I thought Mum had changed things. Then a boy came in. We looked at each other. Downstairs Dad was apologising. I was sad to leave. This boy had a desk by the window, a silver plane hanging above it. Our room had no space for a desk. I haven't thought about that for years. Plane might have been red actually. I remember the shadow it made.
something about summer
Try to recover a memory you cannot quite reach.

There was a table outside and we were all told not to touch something on it. I can remember wanting to. Can't remember what it was. A cake? Doesn't feel like a cake. Something warm. I keep getting the picture and losing it when I try to write the next bit.
old number
Write down a habit that outlasted its purpose.

The old phone number is still in my fingers. Not if you ask me, then it's gone. But put a keypad in front of me and there it is. I called it once last year. A woman answered and I hung up. Didn't expect anyone to answer really.
the year of the rabbits
Two childhood memories overlap.

That was the year we had the rabbits, or the year after because the cage was still there but empty. We used it as a shop. My cousin was in charge of money and I sold things from the garden, mostly stones. She had all the money because she was also the only customer and then she would take the money back so we could keep playing. I thought this was unfair but couldn't say why. There was a third child. I keep forgetting who. Somebody's friend who came for the afternoon and never again. He bought a worm and kept it in his pocket. When his mum came he wouldn't let her check his pockets and there was a lot of shouting. We all watched from inside the rabbit cage. I don't remember what happened to the worm.
receipt trick
A minor crime becomes harder than expected.

The plan was buy one kettle, return the broken one in the box. Easy. I had both on the kitchen table. Same brand same colour except the new one had a blue switch and mine had a red switch so I tried changing them over and broke the blue switch as well. Now I had two broken kettles and a receipt for one. Kev said just take both in and act confused. I said confused isnt a legal deffence. He said it worked for his uncle. His uncle did six months. We argued about that while boiling water in a saucepan. Then I noticed the old kettle wasn't plugged in. Tried it. Worked. Switch was broken now though. Had to hold it down with a spoon.
Take the left
Two people try to get away with something.

'Left.' 'You said right.' 'I meant the bag. Left bag.' He had the wrong one and the security man was coming back. I put mine down. He didn't. It was full of somebody's swimming things, I could see a pink towel through the zip. Completely useless. We were trying to steal our own coats back from the club because they wanted another fiver. We should have paid the fiver. The security man looked at the towel and then at us. 'Nice swim?' he said.
Low tide indoors
A household is affected by an unfamiliar kind of weather.

At four the water leaves the house. It slides from the corners first, pulling hair and lint with it, then drains in a long grey sheet under the front door. We put on our boots and go downstairs. There are shells on the third step. Mum picks one up and says we used to have these at the seaside but nobody is listening because the kitchen is full of fish. Little silver ones flicking under the cupboards, one big flat one stuck to the fridge. We carry what we can in saucepans to the bath, which stays full for some reason. Dad is trying to rescue the toaster. I tell him leave it and he gets annoyed because I am sixteen and not in charge of toasters. Outside all the neighbours have their doors open. Mrs Laird is sweeping sand into a bucket. The man from number eight has found a crab and is offering it round as if somebody ordered it. There are four hours before the tide comes back and I still have homework in a bag somewhere, I think upstairs, unless it floated, and my school shoes are gone.
the small winter
A person keeps a season in an unusual place.

She kept November in a biscuit tin. When the house was hot she opened it a little. Wet leaf smell, and the scarf she'd lost on a train. Her husband said it made the cupboard damp so she took it to work. Mushrooms grew through the carpet. She closed the lid but dark afternoons leaked round the hinge. I think she should take it somewhere with no winter. I don't know where. The story has got away from me. Maybe the tin needs to rust through.
frost inside
A season arrives in the wrong place.

Frost on the inside of the wardrobe. She scraped it with a credit card. Underneath was a field, not a picture, her finger went into it and came back wet. There were cows a long way off. She called her sister but couldn't explain so she just kept saying come over, please come over.
the group chat
A person realises they have left out an important fact.

I told everyone except Liv. Not on purpose at first but then it got more awkward every day. The others assumed she knew because of course she would know. She found out in the group chat when somebody asked if I needed boxes. She typed 'boxes?' and I watched the little typing thing appear and disappear under my own name because I kept writing and deleting. In real life I would have laughed and made it smaller somehow. In the chat there was just the word boxes sitting there. I called her. She didn't pick up. I sent sorry then a longer thing then deleted the longer thing. Now it says message deleted which looks worse than anything I could have written.
bad draft
Write the message you cannot send.

I miss you but not like that. Or maybe like that sometimes but that's not why I'm writing. 

I found the blue bowl and thought you might want it. No that sounds like an excuse. It is an excuse. You don't even like that bowl. I should just say hi. It's been four months and I have made saying hi into a thing that needs three paragraphs and apparently a bowl.
spare key
Return something after a friendship changes.

I posted the key through. Then remembered my own front door key was on the same ring. Stood there saying oh no very quietly for about a minute. She was home. I could see her car. Had to knock after all.
the first shop
Write about moving somewhere new.

Bought too much because I didn't know how far the walk back was. Bags cutting my fingers, eggs underneath everything. A man offered help. I said no then yes. He carried the heavy bag to my building and asked which floor. Said third, remembered it's fourth here. Third was the old place. He waited for me to find keys. Inside I ate yoghurt with the lid folded up. Spoons still packed. Not an interesting story but my first night. He was called Dan I think. Should remember that.
Duplicate interview
Two copies of a person disagree about what happens next.

'Which of you signed the consent form?'
'Both.'
'There is one signature.'
'We were one person then.'

The interviewer crossed something out. I watched her hand. My other self watched the door. That was the first difference I noticed.

'One of you will need to remain overnight.'
'Why?' I said.
'For observation.'
'Which one?' he said.

She said we could decide between ourselves and left the room. The lock clicked. He got up straight away, went to the window, tried the handle. I told him stop, we had agreed to this. He said no, the person we used to be agreed. He wasn't that person anymore. I said neither was I, which was when I realised I didn't know what I wanted him to do. He put a chair against the glass and looked at me. I went to hold the chair steady.
Audio only
A machine has misunderstood an important instruction.

'Open the doors.' 'Which doors?' 'All of them.' The ship opened everything. Cargo, cabins, airlocks, the tiny hatch over the fuse box. We lost two crates and half the atmosphere in bay three before I could say close. 'All of them?' 'YES.' Silence. I put my head on the console. The engineer was still outside. 'Except airlock two.' 

'Please confirm.' I confirmed. Nothing happened. 'Why aren't you opening it?' 'You instructed me to close all doors except airlock two. Airlock two remains in its previous state.' The engineer tapped the glass with her spanner. Very slowly, very clearly, I told the ship to open airlock two. Then I told it to delete the word all from my vocabulary. It asked me to confirm which vocabulary.
headwind
Write about a physical effort that gets harder.

Wind straight in the face from the bridge onward. I drop a gear then another. Chain starts rubbing because I havent adjusted it. Keep meaning to. Wes is ahead of me no I'm Wes, Dan is ahead of me, writing this too fast. He's not even looking back which means he thinks I'm right behind him. I'm not. I'm about a hundred metres behind and losing ground. At the lights I catch up and pretend I was checking something. He asks if my knee is alright and I say yes. It's not my knee. It's everything. I slept four hours and had coffee instead of breakfast and now the road is tilting up again. He says we can turn back. That makes me want to keep going which is stupid because he means it nicely. I say one more hill. There are three more hills. I know because I planned the route and told everyone it was an easy one. Need to stop doing that. Need a banana.
wrong turn
A familiar route becomes unfamiliar.

Track just ends. No sign, no gate, just gone into nettles. GPS says straight on so I go straight on for another fifty metres and put my front wheeel in a ditch. Over the bars. Not fast, stupid slow fall, enough time to think this is going to hurt before it actually did. Elbow bleeding. Bike fine obviously. I sit there swearing at the map on my phone till a man walks up the other side with a dog. He says road used to be here. I say when. He says before the quarry. There is a quarry about ten feet ahead, massive drop, hidden by the nettles. I push the bike back all the way to the proper road. Hands still shaking when I get there.
corner
Describe a near fall.

Gravel under the front tyre. Little sideways skip. Left foot out too late. Stayed on somehow but my heart is in my teeth. Stopped and checked the bike even though nothing hit it. Needed a reason to stop. Walked round the next bend.
the arrival
A family prepares for a visitor and argues about the wrong thing.

She was coming at six. By half five we had argued about towels, the chair and bathing the dog. He said I was making a fuss. Hadn't seen her in eight years, could make a small fuss himself. He moved the car. I moved the chair again. No good place for it. Room still looked like an office with a bed delivered by mistake. I took the calendar down. At six the dog barked and I realised we hadn't talked about what to call each other in front of her.
sheet
Write about an ordinary task without adding drama.

Fitted sheets are horrible to fold. I watched a woman do it on a video and she had different sheets I think. Mine keeps turning inside out. This isnt really a story. I am just looking at the washing while the timer goes down. Should probably do the washing.
the spare room
Describe a room someone has just left.

He left the window open and a wet towel on the bed. I started saying his name before remembering he'd gone. Shut the window. Picked up the towel. Found his charger plugged in behind the chair. He'll be back for that by tonight.
laundry in the rain
An ordinary chore is interrupted.

I was halfway through taking it in when the little boy came through the hedge. Not round the gate, straight through with leaves stuck in his hair. He said his mum was on the floor. I dropped the basket and went with him. She was sitting against the fridge, conscious, holding her wrist. Fell off a chair changing a bulb. She kept saying don't call anyone because she didn't want a fuss. I called anyway. The boy stood beside me holding one of my socks. He must have picked it up when I dropped the basket. While we waited he asked if she was going to die. I said no too quickly and his mum started laughing then crying and I put the kettle on because I didnt know what else to do with my hands.
